Transform CR-Birding data to a Darwin Core Archive

Source: R/write_dwc.R
write_dwc.Rd

Transforms observation data downloaded from CR-Birding to a Darwin Core Archive.

Usage

write_dwc(
  data,
  directory,
  dataset_id = NULL,
  dataset_name = unique(data$animal_project),
  license = NULL,
  rights_holder = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with observation data downloaded from CR-Birding. Data are expected to be in English and from a single study.

directory

Path to local directory to write files to.

dataset_id

Identifier for the dataset.

dataset_name

Title of the dataset. Defaults to animal_project.

license

License of the dataset.

rights_holder

Acronym of the organization owning or managing the rights over the data.

Value

CSV and meta.xml files written to disk. And invisibly, a list of data frames with the transformed data.

Details

The resulting files can be uploaded to an IPT for publication to GBIF and/or OBIS.

Transformation details

This function transforms data to:

  • An Occurrence core.

  • An Extended Measurement Or Facts extension

  • A meta.xml file.

Key features of the Darwin Core transformation:

  • Deployments (animal+ring associations) are parent events, with ringing and resightings as child events. No information about the parent event is provided other than its ID, meaning that data can be expressed in an Occurrence core with one row per observation and parentEventID shared by all occurrences in a deployment.

  • The ringing event often contains metadata about the animal (sex, bird age). Bird age is conservatively mapped to lifeStage, with pullus being mapped to juvenile. Other values are not mapped, as life stage is species-dependent. Sex and bird age are additionally provided in an Extended Measurement Or Facts extension, where values are mapped to a controlled vocabulary recommended by OBIS.

  • Observations without bird_id or with observation_status = "impossible" or "unlikely" are excluded.

  • Parameters are used to set the following record-level terms:

    • dwc:datasetID: dataset_id.

    • dwc:datasetName: dataset_name.

    • dcterms:license: license.

    • dcterms:rightsHolder: rights_holder.

Required data

The source data should have at least the following fields:

  • observation_id

  • observation_date

  • observation_lat

  • obervation_lon

  • bird_species

  • bird_id

  • bird_shorthand

  • observation_is_capture

  • observation_status

Examples

write_dwc(pied_avocet, directory = "my_directory")
#> 
#> ── Transforming data to Darwin Core ──
#> 
#> ── Writing files ──
#> 
#> • my_directory/occurrence.csv
#> • my_directory/meta.xml
#> • my_directory/emof.csv

# Clean up (don't do this if you want to keep your files)
unlink("my_directory", recursive = TRUE)
